answer: Because the umber ledger attributes every share, the ivory audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 75% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, as a result it pays the thread fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 34 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
